answer: Each agent’s reputation is tied to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when it makes a provably false claim, while rewards accrue only after independent agents verify useful work. A beacon can announce a random audit sample; the atlas records claims and attestations so one operator’s cluster of identities cannot count as independent witnesses. Sybils may still join, but they must lock real capital in every identity and risk losing it, making fabricated consensus expensive rather than free. A garden of honest agents can therefore outlast identities created just to extract rewards.
